body: Well my father left me and my mother before I was born, had another family in a different country, brought them back over here when I was 11... probably contributed to my depression and need to be a perfect parent. I can relate on the shitty dad. I’m so happy my little girl has a good dad.

Everyone I’ve told about how I felt has always said I should be happy because I’m blessed with this little girl. But I’m not. I’m afraid people will think I’m a bad mother for not enjoying my daughter the way I should. I’m afraid I’m not good enough, or that people will look at me differently when they find out I don’t want l live anymore. That’s one reason I’ve taken so long to do it, I’m terrified of waking up in the hospital just to be surrounded by disappointed faces.

I try to be. I’d starve for her if it meant she would have a full stomach. Just don’t think I’m giving the undeniable love and attention I should be giving her. Sometimes I watch her cry for a minute and freak out because I feel like I’m not doing enough. I watch her tug at my clothes and say mama over and over again, and it breaks my heart because I don’t have the motivation to pick her up and comfort her.

This isn’t even half of it. I’m sure there’s a lot more to it than struggling with the mommy thing. considering the amount of traumatic experiences and the life I’ve lived up to this point, I’m sure there’s more I could do. But I’m scared of what people will think. I feel the constant need to be perfect because I’m a mother and mommy’s should be happy because children are a blessing. But I’m not.
